title: Greeks Found Cyrene
description: Greek colonists from Thera founded the city of Cyrene in eastern Libya, which became a major center of Hellenic culture and learning.

title: Carthaginian Control of Tripolitania
description: The coastal cities of Tripolitania, including Leptis Magna, flourished under Carthaginian and Phoenician trade networks in the western region.

title: Arab Conquest of Libya
description: Arab armies under Amr ibn al-As conquered the region, bringing Islam and Arabic language to Libya and ending Byzantine rule.

title: Ottoman Conquest of Tripoli
description: The Ottoman Empire captured Tripoli from the Knights of St. John, beginning centuries of Ottoman influence over Libya.

title: Italian Invasion of Libya
description: Italy invaded Ottoman Libya during the Italo-Turkish War, beginning Italian colonial rule that lasted until World War II.

title: Independence of Libya
description: Libya gained independence as the United Kingdom of Libya under King Idris I, becoming the first country to achieve independence through the UN.

title: Gaddafi's Coup
description: Muammar Gaddafi led a military coup that overthrew the monarchy, establishing a republic and ruling Libya for over four decades.

title: Libyan Revolution
description: A popular uprising during the Arab Spring, backed by NATO intervention, led to the fall and death of Muammar Gaddafi.

title: Austronesian Settlement
description: Seafarers from Southeast Asia settled Madagascar, bringing crops, language and culture that shaped the Malagasy people.

title: Portuguese Sight Madagascar
description: Portuguese navigator Diogo Dias became the first European to sight Madagascar, opening the island to European contact.

title: Rise of the Merina Kingdom
description: King Andrianampoinimerina began unifying the central highlands, laying the foundation for the powerful Kingdom of Madagascar.

title: Radama I Recognized as King
description: King Radama I expanded the Merina kingdom over most of the island and welcomed British missionaries who introduced a written Malagasy script.

title: French Colonization
description: France annexed Madagascar as a colony, abolishing the monarchy and exiling Queen Ranavalona III.

title: Malagasy Uprising
description: A major nationalist revolt against French colonial rule was suppressed with heavy loss of life, fueling the independence movement.

title: Independence of Madagascar
description: Madagascar gained full independence from France, becoming the Malagasy Republic with Philibert Tsiranana as its first president.

title: Maravi Kingdom Forms
description: The Maravi Confederacy emerged around Lake Malawi, giving the country its later name and dominating regional trade.

title: Livingstone Reaches Lake Malawi
description: Scottish explorer David Livingstone reached Lake Malawi, drawing European attention to the region and its slave trade.

title: British Central Africa Protectorate
description: Britain established a protectorate over the territory, later known as Nyasaland, bringing colonial administration.

title: Chilembwe Uprising
description: Reverend John Chilembwe led an armed revolt against colonial rule, becoming an enduring symbol of Malawian resistance.

title: Independence of Malawi
description: Nyasaland gained independence as Malawi under Hastings Banda, who later became its long-ruling president.

title: First Multiparty Elections
description: Malawi held its first multiparty democratic elections, ending decades of one-party rule and electing Bakili Muluzi president.

title: Joyce Banda Becomes President
description: Joyce Banda became Malawi's first female president, one of the few women to lead an African nation.

title: Founding of the Mali Empire
description: Sundiata Keita defeated the Sosso and founded the Mali Empire, which grew into one of West Africa's wealthiest states.

title: Mansa Musa's Pilgrimage
description: Emperor Mansa Musa undertook a famous pilgrimage to Mecca, distributing immense gold and showcasing Mali's wealth.

title: Djinguereber Mosque Built
description: Commissioned under Mansa Musa, the Djinguereber Mosque in Timbuktu became a center of Islamic learning and architecture.

title: Songhai Captures Timbuktu
description: The rising Songhai Empire under Sunni Ali captured Timbuktu, eclipsing the declining Mali Empire.

title: French Conquest
description: France captured Timbuktu and incorporated the region into French Sudan, part of French West Africa.

title: Independence of Mali
description: Mali gained independence from France under Modibo Keita, taking its name from the historic medieval empire.

title: Democratic Transition
description: A popular uprising overthrew dictator Moussa Traore, leading to a new constitution and multiparty democracy.

title: Northern Mali Conflict
description: A Tuareg rebellion and Islamist insurgency seized northern Mali, prompting French and international military intervention.

title: Almoravid Movement Begins
description: The Almoravid religious and military movement arose among Sanhaja Berbers in the region, later conquering Morocco and Spain.

title: Almoravids Sack Koumbi Saleh
description: Almoravid forces are said to have captured the capital of the Ghana Empire, reshaping power across the western Sahara.

title: Char Bouba War
description: A thirty-year war among Berber and Arab tribes ended with Arab Hassani dominance, shaping Mauritanian society.

title: French Protectorate
description: France established a protectorate over Mauritania, incorporating it into French West Africa.

title: Independence of Mauritania
description: Mauritania gained independence from France under Moktar Ould Daddah, its first president.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Mauritania became the last country in the world to formally abolish slavery, though the practice persisted afterward.

title: Mauritania-Senegal Border Conflict
description: Ethnic and border tensions erupted into violent conflict with Senegal, causing mass expulsions and displacement.

title: Portuguese Arrival
description: Portuguese sailors became the first Europeans to visit the uninhabited island of Mauritius in the early 16th century.

title: Dutch Claim Mauritius
description: The Dutch took possession of the island and named it after Prince Maurice of Nassau, beginning European settlement attempts.

title: Extinction of the Dodo
description: The flightless dodo bird, found only on Mauritius, became extinct due to hunting and introduced species, a famous symbol of human impact.

title: French Colonization
description: France claimed the island as Isle de France, developing sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans.

title: British Capture Mauritius
description: Britain seized the island during the Napoleonic Wars, restoring the name Mauritius and ruling it for over 150 years.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Slavery was abolished, after which indentured laborers from India were brought to work the sugar estates, reshaping the population.

title: Independence of Mauritius
description: Mauritius gained independence from Britain, with Seewoosagur Ramgoolam becoming its first prime minister.

title: Mauritius Becomes a Republic
description: Mauritius became a republic within the Commonwealth, replacing the British monarch with a president as head of state.

title: Founding of the Idrisid Dynasty
description: Idris I founded the Idrisid dynasty, establishing the first Moroccan Islamic state and the city of Fez.

title: University of al-Qarawiyyin Founded
description: Fatima al-Fihri founded al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, considered the world's oldest continuously operating university.

title: Marrakesh Founded by Almoravids
description: The Almoravids founded Marrakesh as their capital, building a vast empire spanning North Africa and Muslim Spain.

title: Battle of Alcacer Quibir
description: Moroccan forces decisively defeated a Portuguese invasion, killing King Sebastian and preserving Moroccan independence.

title: French and Spanish Protectorates
description: The Treaty of Fez established French and Spanish protectorates over Morocco, ending its full sovereignty.

title: Independence of Morocco
description: Morocco regained independence from France and Spain, with Sultan Mohammed V leading the restored monarchy.

title: The Green March
description: King Hassan II led 350,000 Moroccans into Western Sahara to claim the territory as Spain withdrew.

title: Constitutional Reform
description: Following Arab Spring protests, King Mohammed VI introduced a new constitution expanding parliamentary powers.

title: Swahili Coast Trade
description: Coastal settlements like Sofala became part of the Indian Ocean trade network, exporting gold, ivory and slaves.

title: Vasco da Gama Lands
description: Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama reached the Mozambican coast en route to India, beginning Portuguese involvement.

title: Portuguese Establish Sofala
description: Portugal built a fort at Sofala to control the gold trade, beginning centuries of colonial presence in Mozambique.

title: Mozambique Becomes Separate Colony
description: Portugal made Mozambique a distinct colonial administration, separating it from its Indian holdings.

title: War of Independence Begins
description: The FRELIMO liberation movement launched an armed struggle against Portuguese colonial rule.

title: Independence of Mozambique
description: Mozambique gained independence from Portugal, with Samora Machel becoming its first president.

title: End of the Civil War
description: The Rome General Peace Accords ended a devastating 15-year civil war between FRELIMO and RENAMO.

title: Portuguese Reach the Coast
description: Explorer Diogo Cao reached the Namibian coast, erecting a stone cross at Cape Cross.

title: German South West Africa
description: Germany declared a protectorate over the territory, beginning colonial rule over present-day Namibia.

title: Herero and Nama Genocide
description: German colonial forces carried out a genocide against the Herero and Nama peoples, killing tens of thousands.

title: South African Occupation
description: South Africa took control of the territory during World War I, later administering it under a League of Nations mandate.

title: Namibian War of Independence
description: SWAPO launched an armed struggle against South African rule, beginning a decades-long liberation war.

title: Independence of Namibia
description: Namibia gained independence from South African control, with Sam Nujoma becoming its first president.

title: Germany Recognizes the Genocide
description: Germany officially recognized the colonial-era genocide of the Herero and Nama and pledged development aid.

title: Trans-Saharan Trade Hub
description: Towns like Agadez grew as key stops on trans-Saharan caravan routes carrying gold, salt and goods.

title: Sultanate of Agadez
description: The Tuareg Sultanate of Agadez was established, becoming an important center of trade and Islamic scholarship.

title: Songhai Conquest of Agadez
description: The Songhai Empire under Askia Muhammad annexed Agadez, extending its power into the region.

title: French Colony of Niger
description: France formally established Niger as a colony within French West Africa after suppressing local resistance.

title: Independence of Niger
description: Niger gained independence from France, with Hamani Diori becoming its first president.

title: Uranium Mining Begins
description: Large-scale uranium mining began at Arlit, making Niger one of the world's leading uranium producers.

title: First Democratic Elections
description: Niger held its first free multiparty elections following a national conference and new constitution.

title: Nok Culture Flourishes
description: The Nok civilization in central Nigeria produced sophisticated terracotta sculptures and was among the earliest to smelt iron in the region.

title: Rise of Ife and Igbo-Ukwu
description: The Yoruba city of Ife and the Igbo-Ukwu culture produced renowned bronze and artistic works, marking advanced civilizations.

title: Golden Age of the Benin Empire
description: Under Oba Ewuare, the Kingdom of Benin expanded into a powerful state famed for its bronze plaques and walled city.

title: Sokoto Caliphate Founded
description: Usman dan Fodio led a jihad establishing the Sokoto Caliphate, one of the largest states in 19th-century Africa.

title: Amalgamation of Nigeria
description: Britain merged its northern and southern protectorates into the single colony of Nigeria.

title: Independence of Nigeria
description: Nigeria gained independence from Britain, becoming Africa's most populous nation.

title: Biafran Civil War
description: The southeastern region's secession as Biafra triggered a brutal three-year civil war with widespread famine.

title: Return to Democracy
description: After years of military rule, Nigeria returned to civilian democratic government with the election of Olusegun Obasanjo.

title: Early Kingdom of Rwanda
description: The Kingdom of Rwanda emerged in the Great Lakes region, gradually consolidating power under the Nyiginya dynasty.

title: Reign of Kigeli IV Rwabugiri
description: King Rwabugiri centralized and expanded the Rwandan kingdom, strengthening the monarchy before colonial contact.

title: German Colonial Rule
description: Rwanda became part of German East Africa, with the Germans ruling indirectly through the existing monarchy.

title: Belgian Administration
description: Belgium occupied Rwanda during World War I and later administered it, deepening ethnic divisions through identity policies.

title: Independence of Rwanda
description: Rwanda gained independence from Belgium as a republic, following the abolition of the monarchy.

title: Rwandan Genocide
description: Around 800,000 Tutsi and moderate Hutu were killed in a genocide over roughly 100 days, ended by the RPF's military victory.

title: New Constitution Adopted
description: Rwanda adopted a new constitution and held post-genocide elections, beginning national reconciliation and rebuilding.

title: Takrur and Trans-Saharan Trade
description: The Kingdom of Takrur along the Senegal River became an early Islamic state and important trade center.

title: Jolof Empire Forms
description: The Wolof states united into the Jolof Empire, dominating much of present-day Senegal.

title: Portuguese Reach Senegal
description: Portuguese navigators reached the Senegalese coast, beginning European trade and later the Atlantic slave trade.

title: French Found Saint-Louis
description: France established Saint-Louis at the mouth of the Senegal River, its first permanent settlement in West Africa.

title: Capital of French West Africa
description: Senegal became the administrative heart of French West Africa, with Dakar later serving as its capital.

title: Independence of Senegal
description: Senegal gained independence from France, with poet and statesman Leopold Sedar Senghor as its first president.

title: First Democratic Power Transfer
description: Abdoulaye Wade won the presidency, marking Senegal's first peaceful transfer of power between parties.

title: Portuguese Sight the Islands
description: Portuguese explorers, including Vasco da Gama's fleet, recorded the uninhabited Seychelles islands in the Indian Ocean.

title: French Claim Seychelles
description: France took possession of the islands, naming them after finance minister Jean Moreau de Sechelles.

title: First Permanent Settlement
description: French settlers and enslaved Africans established the first permanent settlement, founding plantation agriculture.

title: British Rule Established
description: The Treaty of Paris formally ceded Seychelles to Britain, beginning over 150 years of British administration.

title: Abolition of Slavery
description: Britain abolished slavery in Seychelles, transforming the islands' plantation society and labor system.

title: Independence of Seychelles
description: Seychelles gained independence from Britain, becoming a republic with James Mancham as its first president.

title: Return to Multiparty Democracy
description: Seychelles adopted a new constitution restoring multiparty democracy after years of one-party socialist rule.
